name: Walnut Creek Library

property.ownership_summary: City-owned library parcel adjoining City civic/park parcel

summary: Post-activation rerun confirms the existing area-specific results: sidewalks, civic plaza/approach, Civic Park and the surface lot are TPF; the ordinary interior and reservable rooms remain federally limited-purpose channels; the underground garage is federally NPF. Remaining California interior/garage labels and cafe control are facility-specific questions, not statewide qualification gaps.
recording_summary: Recording can constitute First Amendment-protected activity. No dedicated public-facing Walnut Creek-specific ordinary-patron camera prohibition was located online. The library-purpose forum classification does not itself create a camera ban; any restriction must be separately sourced and constitutionally tested.
field_items: Exact ambiguous exterior transitions only if enforcement turns on them
open_legal_items: California Speech Clause treatment of the ordinary interior, reservable rooms, underground garage, and garage circulation remains facility-specific

restriction_audits.summary: Recording can be First Amendment-protected activity in this public-access indoor subarea. No material general recording prohibition is established in the current record; any later claimed restriction must identify its legal source and survive the applicable forum, privacy, and activity-specific constitutional analysis.

indoor_common_space.facility_responsibility: The library retains responsibility for safeguarding patron records, account information, staff systems, and other confidential material under laws and policies that apply to the library.
indoor_common_space.visitor_responsibility: A lawful visitor does not assume the library's confidentiality or information-security duties merely by being present. Any visitor duty must arise from law or a constitutionally valid rule that applies directly.
indoor_common_space.recording_effect: Privacy around screens, transactions, or conversations may justify targeted restrictions; it does not itself establish a general camera prohibition in the ordinary public interior.
